Booking’s operating scale — nights, bookings, and the cut

BKNG-unit-econ-2026-09-23 · USD · series 2026-09-23T23:40:00Z · built 2026-09-23 23:36 UTC

The short version

This dig is the operating scoreboard: room nights, gross bookings (the dollar value of travel booked), and take rate (revenue divided by those gross bookings). Merchant means Booking collects the customer’s payment. Agency means the supplier collects, and Booking earns a commission. Income, earnings, and the trailing multiple already live on the key-metrics page. This page does not redo them. Latest quarter: 325 million room nights, $51.0 billion of gross bookings, take rate about 14.4%.

Booking Desk · Latent capital · as of the quarter ended June 30, 2026

How big the machine is

Second quarter 2026 was 325 million room nights. A year earlier the same quarter was 309 million, so nights were up about 5%. The count runs from the third quarter of 2014, through the 2020 collapse, and back to a new high.

The year view runs from 2015 through 2025. Full-year 2025, as Booking printed it, was 1,235 million room nights. Full-year 2024 was 1,144 million. For 2015 through 2022 the year bar is the four quarters added together, because those releases were not used as a single full-year print. For 2023 through 2025 the bar is the company’s own year figure. Hatched bars are the added years.

Gross bookings in the second quarter of 2026 were $51.0 billion, about 9% above the $46.7 billion booked a year earlier. Dollars grew faster than nights. Full-year 2025 gross bookings were $186.1 billion, against $165.6 billion in 2024. Gross bookings include taxes and fees and are net of cancellations, on Booking’s definition.

Who collects the money

Of the $51.0 billion booked in the second quarter of 2026, $37.0 billion was merchant and $14.0 billion was agency. Full-year 2025 was $130.0 billion merchant and $56.1 billion agency, out of $186.1 billion. Agency dollars have been falling in recent years while the total has kept rising. The two legs together are the total.

The mix has moved one way for a long time. Merchant was about 26% of gross bookings in the second quarter of 2019 and about 73% in the second quarter of 2026. The line below is that share, merchant bookings divided by the total.

The same shift shows up in revenue. In the second quarter of 2026 merchant revenue was about $5.13 billion, agency revenue about $1.90 billion, and advertising and other $322 million. Those three lines add to $7.35 billion, which is the same revenue as the income statement for the quarter. Nothing was plugged to make them match.

What Booking keeps

Take rate in the second quarter of 2026 was about 14.4%: $7.35 billion of revenue on $51.0 billion of gross bookings. A year earlier the same quarter was about 14.6%. Full-year 2025 was about 14.5%, which is $26.9 billion of revenue on $186.1 billion of gross bookings. The ratio is seasonal. Recent first quarters sit near 10%. Third quarters run in the high teens. Second and fourth quarters sit in the mid-teens. Across the full history the range is wider because 2020 and 2021 were not normal years. The useful comparison is the recent mid-teens, not the pandemic spike. Where either revenue or gross bookings is missing, the ratio is left blank. The first two quarters of the night series have no ratio for that reason.

Gross bookings per room night were about $157 in the second quarter of 2026, against about $151 a year earlier. It is a rough check on price, mix, and currency in the booking pool. It is not an average daily rate. Booking does not print an average-daily-rate level, only an occasional constant-currency change, and those changes are not drawn here as if they were a price.

Marketing, when Booking prints it as a percent of gross bookings, has recently run from about 3.8% to 4.7%. The second quarter of 2026 was 4.7%. The chart starts in the fourth quarter of 2024, which is the first quarter in this file. Earlier years are omitted. They are not connected with a line through empty history.

Flight tickets and rental-car days are printed in the same table as room nights, and the history is full enough to draw. They are a side business next to stays. In the second quarter of 2026 Booking printed 17 million flight tickets and 23 million rental-car days.

Where the map stops

The earnings tables are company totals. Booking prints constant-currency growth for the whole company. It does not print room nights, gross bookings, or revenue as levels for Europe, Asia, or the Americas. Those regional stacks are blank. A growth rate is not turned into an invented regional dollar.

Two other levels are blank for the same reason. The share of Booking.com room nights that are alternative accommodations is not printed as a level. Adjusted EBITDA is not in this dig. Income, earnings, and the trailing multiple stay on the key-metrics page, including the weeks when trailing earnings nearly vanished. There is no price on this page.
